hard_anchors: Deterministic short-term structure is coherent descending, with a Lower High Lower Low sequence and no confirmed breakout or breakdown.
Deterministic long-term structure is also descending, although it is classified as an early bull-reversal transition risk state.
The latest close is below the fast, intermediate, and medium moving-average references supplied, preserving a bearish moving-average hierarchy.
Recent price is at the lower edge of the short-horizon range and immediately adjacent to support, consistent with negative impulse but also elevated support-test sensitivity.
Short-horizon ATR is below longer-horizon ATR and ATR14 is moderate relative to price, indicating normal and moderating realized volatility rather than a fresh volatility shock.
Volume is below its 20-session average for each of the latest three sessions, indicating persistent volume contraction.
Bullish clustered-lows patterns identify durable support, while a bearish fair-value-gap and bearish peak pattern align locally with the descending structure.
event_modifiers: No concrete scheduled or unscheduled event was supplied as dominant within the current classification horizon.

narrative_residual: The research recommendation, fundamental advocacy, and conditional portfolio language are excluded from state determination.
Bullish and bearish rhetorical framing is retained only as non-determinative residual commentary.
contradictory_signals: Triple-bottom and double-bottom detections at clustered lows raise reversal potential against the active lower-high/lower-low sequence.
The long-term early bull-reversal risk label conflicts partially with the still-descending long-term deterministic trend.
Price is near support, so continuation evidence has less room before a possible mean-reversion response.
Soft participation weakens confirmation of the current negative impulse.

market_state.state_summary: AAPL is in a coherent, aligned descending environment across higher, trading, and lower timeframes. Negative impulse is supported by price below the supplied moving-average hierarchy and placement near the lower end of the recent range. Volatility is normal and moderating, while three consecutive below-average volume readings indicate contracting participation. Clustered swing-low support and reversal-pattern detections create material mean-reversion and reclassification risk, but do not yet displace the active descending structure.
key_risks: Clustered swing-low support creates elevated reversal sensitivity.
Soft volume reduces confirmation of bearish continuation.
A sustained failure of the lower-high/lower-low sequence would reclassify the trading-timeframe state.
Bearish fair-value-gap interaction can increase short-horizon whipsaw.
Long-term transition evidence conflicts with the active descending structure.
